canonical_statement: Every nonempty partially ordered set in which every nonempty chain has an upper bound has a maximal element.
canonical_statement_status: exact nonempty-carrier/nonempty-chain Lean statement self-tested pending master acceptance; primary-source H0 remains open

canonical_formal_target.environment_fingerprint: Lean 4.29.0@98dc76e3; mathlib@8a178386; exact hashes in statement.json

domain_and_universes: universe u; alpha : Type u with PartialOrder alpha and Nonempty alpha; a chain is c : Set alpha satisfying IsChain (fun x y => x <= y) c.
quantifiers: for every type alpha with a partial order
for every chain c in alpha
there exists an upper bound of c in alpha
there exists a maximal element m of alpha
ordered_binders: for every nonempty chain, its BddAbove hypothesis
hypotheses: the relation is a partial order
every chain has an upper bound in the carrier
conclusion: There exists m in the carrier such that no strictly larger carrier element exists (equivalently, m is maximal).
excluded_degenerate_cases: An empty carrier is excluded in the ordinary nonempty-poset formulation
An upper bound outside the carrier is not sufficient for a subset formulation
A greatest element is not required
A maximum of each chain is not required
Preorders are not silently substituted for partial orders in the canonical human claim

alternate_encodings.target: all chains, including the empty chain, are bounded above
alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent candidate because an upper bound for the empty chain supplies an inhabitant
more general library formulation whose maximality conclusion specializes to an order

alternate_encodings.target: maximal member of a subset closed under chain upper bounds
alternate_encodings.relationship: relativized formulation requiring membership predicates and an internal upper bound
